**Finding: Compliant** — no redline required.

The agreement imposes no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation on Sparkling, so we retain full freedom to buy from other suppliers. Specifically:

- **Section 2 (Grant)** — the licence is expressly "non-transferable and non-exclusive," a limit on our licence scope, not an exclusive-dealing covenant.
- **Section 3 (Restrictions on Use)** — confined to copying, assignment/sublicensing, reverse engineering and scope-of-use; no bar on procuring competing software or services from third parties.
- **Section 10 (Maintenance and Support)** — obliges Garman to deliver updates, telephone support and repair services on a renewable one-year term; it does not require us to source support, Improvements or future modules solely from Garman.
- **Section 11 (Fees)** — payment per the Fee Schedule only, with no minimum-purchase or requirements commitment.

The remaining occurrences of "exclusive" are benign and unrelated to sourcing: "exclusive remedy" (§15), the non-exclusive escrow licence (§16), and non-exclusive jurisdiction (general provisions). Targeted searches for "sole," "requirements," "purchase," "procure," "supplier," "competing" and "exclusivity" surfaced nothing in the nature of exclusive dealing.

This satisfies the playbook's preferred position, so no change is proposed. Worth noting for negotiation awareness: if Garman later seeks to add sole-source language for support or future modules, our fallback is exclusivity capped at a defined product category and 12 months, terminating automatically on Garman's failure to meet service levels or delivery dates.
